Pretty general, but im just curious what advice you guys may have for this. Im in college, i want to get a part time job so i can start saving for a car. Just looking for any good advice or just perspective from some of you guys because I know some of yall are pretty well put together. Thanks
Whats your advice for someone about to get a job to save up for a car?

Buy a used car, something that you can afford and save up some money to fix the used car. So if you save like 5 grand then use 3grand for the car and the other 2 grand for repairs. You will have a reliable vehicle. Don't get sucked into vehicle payments. If you can do the maintenance and repairs yourself. Go to the mechanic for the more technical repairs.

Set a budget for a vehicle, and start looking at what fits within your budget as soon as you get a job - don't be picky. This way, you'll have a better idea of what kind of car you can afford and maybe spot a good deal. You'll also have some tools for bartering if you have several cars in mind with similar features/mileage but different prices. Good mileage on a car is anywhere between 12-15k miles per year since manufacturing. Higher mileage = cheaper car, but you could face possibly replacing the transmission or something else more expensive sooner rather than later. As far as saving for a car, come with a plan that works for you - everyone is a little different about this.

When buying a used car, have the finances already in place. Even if you decide you need a loan, go to your bank/credit union and get pre-approved rather than finance through a dealership. You'll save on interest, and have more leverage when negotiating. Only buy a new car from a dealership - like brand new. Used cars, find an independent owner. If you do end up at a dealership, wait until the end of the month, when they have to really move inventory, they'll be more flexible with negotiating.

You can pay for a carfax, which is like $50, and most car servicing places report oil changes and other maintenance - sometimes the owner will pay for the carfax. Beware of a newer vehicle with nothing reported, this means the owner did things themselves, and could have been in an unreported wreck (happened to me with a trade-in, long story).

So, have the money you want to spend, get a carfax, and look up the blue book value on kbb.com so you know what you should reasonably pay for it. Obviously test-drive it. If you can, take it to a mechanic while test-driving to have them look over it. Also, be prepared to pay sales tax and licensing fees, property taxes and maintenance. Like, don't buy a used mercedes because just an oil change will be outrageous compared to a honda. If you have to have a loan to buy a car, you'll have to get full coverage insurance, which is more expensive so keep that in mind.

Good luck, hope this helps!
Research your car. Don't buy a lemon or something out of your budget. Don't forget to factor in insurance and drivers permit costs.

You're going to want something nice, but don't do it. Don't take on a car payment if you don't have to; you probaqbly have more important expenses right now. Find something inexpensive but reliable, probably a used car from late 90s or early 2000s. For example, if you can find a civic or corolla that has only been under 1 or 2 owners and doesn't look modified, that could be a reliable option. I wouldn't buy a car for much more than $3500 as your first car, unless you are pretty flush with funds.
